notes:
I couldn't write these notes because my research tools stopped working before I could read any sources. My first attempt to fetch the commentary pages (Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary, Benson, Matthew Henry and the NET Bible notes on Hosea 5) hit the tool-use limit. My second attempt was refused, and no more tool calls are allowed in this turn. So I haven't read a single page.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I found nothing, the honest result is no notes. I haven't written a commentary from memory, because that would break the rule against filling gaps from my own knowledge, and I couldn't show where any of it came from.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll go through the sources one or two at a time so I don't hit the limit:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word (Hosea 5), Precept Austin's Hosea 5 commentary, and Bible Hub's Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit, Benson and Matthew Henry entries.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** a targeted search of Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon, GTY, Ligonier, LCMS and 1517. Verse 15 ("until they admit their guilt and seek My face") and verse 4 ("Their deeds do not permit them to return") are the likeliest places for Reformed and Wesleyan views to differ.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes (especially on v. 7 "New Moon," v. 8 "Beth-aven," v. 11 "worthless idols" and v. 13 "the great king"), Bible Odyssey, and New Advent's Haydock or Church Fathers material on Hosea.

If you can paste text from any of those pages, I can also start on the notes straight away from that, with the URLs.
